previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: The legacy point lay approximately 2.64 kilometres east of the named Gjellestad archaeological site and had no identifiable source object.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The georadar-discovered ship grave and associated settlement and burial landscape on Viksletta, interpreted together with the surviving monumental mound Jellhaugen approximately 175.6 metres to the south.
identity.identityProblem: The record combines a buried ship grave, a broad georadar landscape and a separate visible mound. One marker cannot be treated as the complete geometry of all archaeological remains.
identity.splitReason: The ship grave, settlement remains and Jellhaugen form one coherent Gjellestad interpretation record. The main coordinate follows the ship-discovery field, while Jellhaugen is retained as a secondary anchor.

requiredEvidence: explicit rejection of locality and visitor-infrastructure points

evidence.sourceName: OpenStreetMap node 5985030252 – Viking ship and settlements remains
evidence.finding: The named archaeological-site point is at 59.14857, 11.25038 and represents the Gjellestad ship and settlement-remains field.
evidence.reason: Directly represents the archaeological discovery area rather than a farm locality, mound, sign or parking point.

evidence.finding: NIKU documents the 2018 motorised georadar discovery of an approximately 20-metre ship form around half a metre below the topsoil, together with graves and buildings in the surrounding field.
evidence.reason: Confirms the discovery identity, method and wider archaeological scope.

evidence.finding: The county documents the 2020–2021 excavation, the poorly preserved ship timbers, approximately 1,300 rivets, thousands of fragments and the relationship to the wider Gjellestad landscape.
evidence.reason: Confirms the physical ship-grave context and archaeological interpretation.

evidence.sourceName: Antiquity – Gjellestad: a newly discovered central place in south-east Norway
evidence.finding: The study interprets Gjellestad as a central place with monumental graves, buildings and long-term elite activity rather than an isolated ship burial.
evidence.reason: Supports the landscape-level identity of the combined record.

evidence.finding: The digital interpretation connects the ship grave, Jellhaugen, burial mounds, longhouses and the wider central-place landscape.
evidence.reason: Confirms the public interpretation model and distinction between individual monuments.

evidence.finding: The surviving mound has a representative point at 59.14704, 11.25114, approximately 175.6 metres south of the applied ship-grave anchor.
evidence.reason: Valid secondary anchor and landscape cross-check, but a separate monument from the ship grave.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate lies approximately 2,635.7 metres east of the archaeological site.
evidence.reason: Replaced because it does not represent the ship grave, Jellhaugen or the documented central-place landscape.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named ship-grave and settlement-remains anchor and retained the 360-metre gameplay radius. Continue with Høytorp fort.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 2.64 kilometres west.
The ship-grave and settlement-remains field is the primary anchor.
Jellhaugen is a separate secondary anchor approximately 175.6 metres south.
The wider central-place landscape extends beyond the gameplay radius.
The radius is not an excavation, georadar, archaeological, protection or property boundary.
